plan.what_was_built:
The three plan files for the option B usefulness test are written. Status of all three: PROPOSED, not sealed, nothing run. I called no AWS and no outside model, opened no key file, changed no other project file, and ran no git command that changes state. I ran only small standard-library scripts for counting, hashing and checking.

1. 08_OPTION_B_PLAN_v1_0.md (92,985 bytes, sha256 db5c5aaaae80ad6f43344ca49fe148638c393ce6c6330b263ae8922df59d4530). The pre-registration in plain English, 25 sections. It covers every item the task listed, including the D1 to D10 section, a section of details fixed where the design was open, and the owner questions with defaults. Canon definition lines are not retyped anywhere; examples use placeholders.

2. optionb/PLAN_CONSTANTS.json (59,702 bytes, sha256 b3588a0d888a0c638ba6e8aa7e280f26f10134c0baa3e93f79bf6864323ea81d). Valid JSON, ASCII only. It holds every seed, threshold, wording, list, limit and code a program needs. Multi-line texts are lists of lines joined with LF. Placeholders look like <<NAME>> and are filled by plain replacement.

3. optionb/FILE_FORMATS.md (77,121 bytes, sha256 dbcc2cdf477a385e47b8123631f0556c446a489569a02cb45e229887d1f422a9). The schema of every file between programs, in pipeline order, with writer, readers and one small example each. It also fixes the package layout, the five runner commands, the seal steps and the small rules two programs must apply the same way.

Checks I ran on the outputs (all passed): all three files use LF and UTF-8; the constants file parses; every brief, frame, closing wording, word list, practice and reserve setting, outcome code, stop code and report sentence in the constants appears word for word in the plan; all 32 JSON examples in the formats file parse; every section cross-reference resolves; the patterns in the constants compile; the canon-line pattern matches exactly 10 lines of guide Part A; no canon definition text appears in any of the three files; no 'CO-' appears; ROLE-PLAIN appears only as struck.

deviations_from_design_and_why: D1 applied: ROLE-PLAIN removed everywhere. Call counts recomputed. Fixed rule (g) and the ROLE-PLAIN printed lines are struck. The plan states that a miss can no longer be split into 'information did not help' and 'notation was not read'.
Pairing rule fixed as: team A entries in file order, first unused matching team B entry. Reason: simplest exact rule; measured to give the same counts as the largest pairing.
Exclusion test reads the raw entries of both teams (before cleaning). Reason: the stricter reading; same 104 passages.

Role-note details fixed: 'shorter' is by characters with ties to team A; ^1 lines first and then the others, each in passage order (this matches the design's Example 3); a sentence rule with a guard for Mr, Mrs, Ms, Dr, Prof, St, Jr, Sr; only an identical supporting quote gets the 'same as' line.

Form ids introduced (MEET_AGAIN ... NEW_STARTER) so the blind writer never sees type names such as LAND. The option check for both PULL-PUSH forms looks at left-over ^2 and ^3 entries. Reason: that is how the design counted left-overs per type, and it is the stricter reading.

The full question brief was composed by me from the design's fixed phrases, because the design gave only its parts. I added one format sentence: 'The right option must not stand out by its length.' The owner has not read it.

Forbidden-word matching fixed: list A matches a word and its longer forms (as the passage tool did); list B matches whole words in any letter case, so 'above' and 'below' are barred too; list C applies to the question text only. Anchors are compared after curly quotes and white space are normalised.
Plain-fact questions also go through the form check (four options, no anchor), the key check and the no-passage check. Reason: the design did not say; this is the stricter reading.

A spare question is used only after a Step 2 or Step 3 drop of the first question, not after a solver drop and not when the first pass wrote none. Reason: those two steps are the ones the design titles 'by program'; one solver round keeps the Claude export and import simple.
No-passage solvers must pick a letter (no 'more than one fits' escape). An unreadable solver reply counts as 'not picked'. Reason: stricter screen.

Selection fixed as an exact seeded algorithm. The length backstop counts 'single longest' and 'single shortest' apart, each at most 35%, per set, and runs before letters are set. Reason: a combined 35% cap would sit near chance.

Letters are set in tools/ob_assemble.py after the answer-leak screen, not at selection. Keys are therefore sealed in two parts: text keys at seal 3A/3C, lettered keys at seal 5. Reason: the design says letters are set 'after everything else is frozen', and later passage drops would break the letter balance.

Ordinary notes: word target formula N = (percent x C_role x W_p + 50 x M_p) // (100 x M_p); one fixed format line in the request ('Reply with the notes only, as plain text. No heading.'); one fixed sentence in the rewrite request; a second support failure drops the passage for every group.

Support check (D6): a batch is the six notes of two passages; a passage is never split between checkers; the Claude fallback is allowed 24 hours after the first daily-cap stop if notes are still unchecked; an item still unreadable after one more ask counts as FAIL. I wrote the support-check brief; the design only described it.

Answer-leak screen made exact: three letter patterns; rule (b) also tests any question sentence of 5 or more words; all three lengths of both ordinary notes are screened; for program-built notes only the frame text is tested.

Padding made exact: token count without special tokens; target is the largest block with the shortest padding line; the whole padding line counts as padding; the 10% average is worked out for practice passages and final passages apart and either one stops the job. Reason: at least as strict as one pooled average.
Frames fixed where the design was silent: the NO-PASSAGE prompt starts with 'Answer the question.'; the ANSWER-GIVEN note is 'The right answer to the question is <letter>.'

Practice calls fixed as steps P1, P2, P3 with an early stop before P3. Gate 4 counts all practice tasks of a group together. Gate 7 uses the mean seconds of the must-run practice calls. Gate 6 uses the exact 1/6 plus 15 points (31.67%), not the rounded 31.7%.
_EXPLORATORY is added only to codes 5 to 10. Codes 1 to 4 never carry it. Reason: the design's own hand-worked codes show INVALID_RUN and UNINFORMATIVE_DIFFICULTY without the ending on a small set.

Test procedure made exact: at most 5,000 of 100,000 flips; whole-number sums and point rules; a fresh numpy PCG64 generator per test; range from sorted resamples at index 250 and 9749; standard error is the standard deviation of the resamples.

The five made-up sets are defined exactly and each now also has an expected gate result (GATE_STOP_DIFFICULTY, GATE_STOP_DIFFICULTY, GO with wording 1 and level 1, any listed result, GATE_STOP_DIFFICULTY). In DESIGNED, ANSWER-GIVEN is all right and NO-PASSAGE all wrong, otherwise the gate program could not reach GO.

Every runner command exits 0 unless it crashes, and the score command always writes RESULT.json, with the stop code after a stop. Reason: the guest kills later stages on a non-zero exit, and one result file keeps its reader simple.

Pre-check binding added (D7): the pre-check prints the hash of the prompt-hash list and of the padding plan; they go into seal step 7; Gate 0 of the GPU job must print the same values or stop with GATE_STOP_SELFTEST. The two job files are written with no time and no host name so their bytes match.
Pre-check job limits are my proposal (2.00 USD, 60 minutes), because D7 named none.
A tenth added scorer example (a cut-off reply is CUT_OFF) beside the design's nine.

No fallback question writer in this version (the design named Codex/GPT by hand-off). Reason: D4 says each set is written by one model and the tool waits for the next day. Writer temperature set to 1.0 and one retry for an unreadable reply, as the passage tool did.
The 'checked label' heading point, the stricter 'nothing left over' choice and the 4 sub-views are kept as designed. R2 and R3 are kept as 5 points AND the test (D9).

result.what_was_built:
Three small standard-library tools. All three parse, hold LF line ends only, and are plain ASCII. No AWS call, no outside model call, no key file opened, no git change, no seal written for real. The sealed sources still have their pinned hashes.

1. tools/ob_eligibility.py (sha256 73455eef7ce2a7157aad87e42b33a8610b551b0eb4aae7e56feb19aa9db0d104).
- It checks the size and sha256 of the two label files, the hidden-kinds passage file and tools/verdict.py against PLAN_CONSTANTS.json. It refuses on any difference.
- It loads the frozen functions from tools/verdict.py like this: it reads the bytes once, checks their sha256, then compiles and runs those same bytes as a private module named ob_frozen_verdict. So the code that was hashed is the code that runs. verdict.py keeps its report run behind `if __name__ == '__main__':`, so loading it reads nothing, writes nothing and prints nothing. Nothing is copied or re-implemented.
- It applies the rule-15 exclusion on the raw entries of both teams, pairs clear entries one to one in file order with same_span and same_field, opens forms, computes the per-passage ceiling (with the LAND rule), draws the split with seed 20261005 and checks it gives the settings named in the plan, bars V009 and V076, and marks every K1 to K5 passage as one the writer is sent.
- It prints every count beside the plan or design value. It writes elig/exclusions.json and elig/eligibility.json only if every gating count matches. It refuses to write into the real folder once a seal exists.
- Dry run into optionb/dry/: exit 0, ELIGIBILITY_OK. Every count the plan pins matched. The four design entry totals matched.

2. tools/ob_role_notes.py (sha256 c6212ec967f8aebf0430959f2f0c160edc12a6f42671fd3649740fc5a785d386).
- It reads the canon lines from Part A of 02_LABELING_GUIDE_v1_2.md at run time, after a hash check. The file holds no definition text. It writes ^1 to ^9, never CO-n.
- For each of the 192 eligible passages it builds the ROLE, MIXED and QUOTES-ONLY texts and their frame-blanked forms, exactly by the templates in PLAN_CONSTANTS.json: canon lines in number order, ^1 lines first, then entries in passage order, the `same as for "..."` back-reference, no heading, the MIXED swap table.
- It writes notes_role/role_notes.json, notes_role/owner_sample_20.json and OWNER_SAMPLE_ROLE_NOTES.md (20 passages drawn with seed 20261016).
- A real run needs seal step 1 and is refused once seal step 2 exists. A dry run (--dry-run DIR) needs no seal and may not point at the real optionb folder.
- It stops if the fixed frame words of any note hit the answer-leak patterns.
- Dry run into optionb/dry/: exit 0, ROLE_NOTES_OK.

3. tools/ob_seal.py (sha256 7e7ed0823e6e4671475019e06556e8275093bf9e6e0d1609e8e80d8f2110581d).
- Append-only seal file optionb/SEAL_OPTIONB.jsonl, one line per step, in the line format of FILE_FORMATS.md section 15, with the sha256 of the line before.
- Commands: `step 1|2|3A|3B|3C|4|5|6|7` (with --dry-run), `verify`, `status`. Other programs can call ob_seal.require_steps(project, [...]).
- Every step refuses when it is not the next step, when it was already written, when the chain is broken, when any earlier sealed file is missing or changed, or when one of its own files is missing, empty or half written. Step 1 also refuses if any question file exists.
- It was tried only in a scratch copy tree, with made-up stand-in files for the later steps. REAL: 60 of 60 trial checks passed. On the real folder only `status` and a refused `step 1 --dry-run` were run. No real seal line exists.

The owner sample optionb/OWNER_SAMPLE_ROLE_NOTES.md (sha256 b923ecc3e74d2d769eb851a8b8e84febafc84e612550c10301231b5a003e75fa) is a byte copy of the dry-run sample. Its first line says DRY RUN, not sealed.

open_issues: COUNT THAT DIFFERS (gates nothing). The design text says '12 passages open only one form'. REAL: 9 final passages open exactly one form. 12 final passages can carry only one task. The other 3 (V087, V095, V383) open both LAND forms but hold one agreed ^4 entry, so the LAND rule allows one task. The plan's own wording ('12 of them can carry only one') and the ceiling of 300 are right. The design sentence is loose. No rule was bent.

The design says the ROLE note quotes 41.4% of a passage's sentences. REAL with the plan's sentence rule: 41.8%. REAL with the title guard off: 41.45%. So the design figure was measured before the plan added the rule that a full stop after Mr, Dr and the like does not end a sentence. The two other design checks on the notes match exactly (69 and 44).

The design estimated ROLE length as 'about 55 to 197 words, median about 112' by taking an '11-word heading' off 66 / 123 / 208. That heading has 12 words. REAL: 54 / 111 / 196, which is 66 / 123 / 208 minus 12.

FILE_FORMATS.md gives the FILLER base text no field in notes_role/role_notes.json. I did not add one. The tool builds it from prompt.filler_sentence, screens it, prints its size, and offers filler_base_text(). It reaches the job through prompt_parts 'notes.FILLER', which ob_assemble writes. If the plan wants it stored with the role notes, FILE_FORMATS.md needs a field.

PLAN_CONSTANTS.json holds no list of seal steps and their files, and no package list. ob_seal.py codes both from FILE_FORMATS.md sections 14 and 15. If those sections change, ob_seal.py must change too.

ob_seal.py refuses more than the task text asked. Each extra refusal follows a plan rule, but the operator may want to overrule one: step 2 refuses if a question file exists; steps 3A and 3B refuse if a final question file exists; 3A and 3C refuse if that set's ordinary notes already exist or the writer state is not complete or names another model than the plan; 3B refuses when floor_met is not true; step 4 refuses when a passage is still UNCHECKED or REWRITE_NEEDED; step 5 refuses when launch_floor_met is not true or tier is NO_LAUNCH; step 7 refuses unless the pre-check status is SELFTEST_PASS and package_matches_seal passed.

The task named seal steps 1 to 6. FILE_FORMATS.md says tools/ob_seal.py also writes step 7, so I built it: `step 7 --selftest-json FILE --source-zip FILE`. It records exactly the five values of section 15.

The 'question file exists' rule does not look inside the scratch folder optionb/dry/. Files there with question-file names are counted, printed and recorded in the step's values. Other builders' dry runs would otherwise block seal step 1. If the operator wants the stricter reading, the scratch folder must be emptied first and one line in ob_seal.py changed.

The later seal steps (3A to 7) were tried only on made-up stand-in files. The real files do not exist yet. Their checks read these fields of other builders' files, as FILE_FORMATS.md defines them: writer_state 'complete' and 'model'; selection 'practice_setting_count', 'counts', 'floor'; split_fixed 'practice_setting_count', 'floor_met'; support_results 'passages[].status'; removal_log 'launch_floor_met', 'tier', 'final_counts'; and 'inputs' in every JSON file. A builder who names these differently will be refused.

Step 1 'values' holds four small facts beyond the two FILE_FORMATS.md names (excluded_passages, eligible_passages, pinned_sources_checked, question_like_files_in_scratch_folder). Step 1 checks all 13 pinned sources, and hashes the five of plan section 3 as files.
The laptop tools' own hashes are not sealed as files in any step. They appear only in each output file's 'made_by' and, for role notes, in 'inputs'.

result.what_was_built:
Four laptop tools. They are plain Python, standard library only. They follow optionb/FILE_FORMATS.md sections 4 to 7 and read every number and wording from optionb/PLAN_CONSTANTS.json. Nothing was sealed. No outside service was called. No AWS call was made. No key file was opened.

1. tools/ob_write_questions.py (Step 1, the question writer).
- It sends the question brief and up to 8 fenced passages per call to the writer model named in the constants (gemini-2.5-flash for both sets).
- Arguments: --set practice|final, --pass p1|p2 (p2 is the spare pass, with its own seeded batch order), --batch-size (1 to 8), --max-calls (the call budget for the day; 0 writes the plan only), --practice-settings 8..12.
- Blindness: the prompt is built by build_prompt(), which is given only (passage id, passage text) pairs. The tool opens elig/eligibility.json, keeps id, text, setting, setting_role and writer_asks, and drops the rest at once. Every prompt is also tested and the run stops if a prompt holds a Noetic tag or a kind tag.
- Checkpoint and resume: the call log is the record. The checkpoint is rebuilt from the log at every start, so a crash can not cause an extra try. A reply that is not a readable JSON array is asked for once more, then the batch is UNREADABLE. HTTP 429 at the daily cap stops cleanly, is not counted as a try, and the stop time is recorded.
- One model per set: the tool refuses a checkpoint that names another model. There is no model argument.
- Reserve rule guard: a reserve setting can be added to practice only after select/selection_practice.json shows the floor was missed with one setting fewer. No practice wave is added after select/split_fixed.json exists. No final question is written before it exists.
- Every call is logged: model, wave, batch, passage ids, prompt hash, reply hash, full prompt, raw reply.

2. tools/ob_check_questions.py (Steps 2 and 3).
- Form check with all 16 reason codes. Anchor check and option check with the looser word test, run from the hashed bytes of tools/verdict.py. List A is compared with line 19 of tools/write_verdict_passages.py and the tool stops if they differ.
- Writes form_check, anchor_check, option_check and candidates. Candidates hold no label information. The spare (p2) question is used only where a p1 question for that form existed and was dropped by Step 2 or 3.
- It needs both passes complete for exactly the passages of the set. It prints the survival count after each filter.

3. tools/ob_solve_blind.py (Steps 4 and 5).
- Commands: deepseek, export, import, decide.
- deepseek: one item per stateless call, temperature 0, options in a seeded shuffled order per solver and mode. Reply must be one JSON object with the single key answer: one shown letter, or MORE_THAN_ONE or NONE (flags only with the passage). A repeated key is unreadable. HTTP 429, 401, 402 or 403 stops cleanly; the call log is the checkpoint.
- export: writes a plain text sheet for the Claude Sonnet sub-agent. It holds neutral item ids, the passage (Step 4 only), the question and lettered options. No key, no form name, no label, no note, no real passage id. The tool tests the sheet text and refuses to write it if a question id or a form name is in it.
- import: reads the answer sheet once. A missing item, a repeated item, a line that does not fit or a reply that is not allowed counts as unreadable. A sheet whose lines name no item of that sheet is refused. A second, different answer file for the same sheet is refused.
- decide: applies the plan's rule. Keep only if both solvers picked the right option with the passage and neither raised a flag. Drop if both picked the right option with no passage. It refuses while any answer is missing.

4. tools/ob_select.py (Step 6).
- select: at most two role-step questions per passage, different forms, different right things (looser word test), LAND rule, different types preferred, choice drawn with random.Random('<selection>|<passage id>'). One plain-fact question per passage. The 35 percent longest and 35 percent shortest backstop with seeded, logged drops. It writes select/selection_<set>.json (tasks and the key as text; no letters) and a report file select/survival_<set>.json with the survival table for all eight filters.
- It applies the reserve rule and the launch floor and prints GO or the stop reason: STOP_PRACTICE_FLOOR_NOT_MET_MOVE_NEXT_RESERVE_SETTING (it names the next reserve setting) or STOP_DO_NOT_LAUNCH.
- fix-split: writes select/split_fixed.json once, after seal step 3A. The history rows are worked out again from the same files.

All four tools check optionb/SEAL_OPTIONB.jsonl first (needed steps exist, chain intact, every sealed file unchanged) and refuse to write a set that is already sealed.

Dry run. On a made-up fixture of three made-up passages, 36 commands were run in a row from an empty fixture and every one ended as designed. The chain covered: a daily-cap stop and resume, an unreadable reply with one re-ask, a spare question taking the place of a dropped first question, a reserve setting moving to practice, two Claude sheets per mode, a flag, unreadable replies, the practice set being fixed, and the final set through to selection. The fixture results say nothing about real questions.

FORMAT GAP: select/survival_<set>.json is not in FILE_FORMATS.md. It is a report for people and no program reads it. The plan needs survival numbers at the practice step, long before ob_assemble.py runs. As read in tools/ob_seal.py, seal steps 3A and 3C will include it because its name carries the set.

PLAN RULE DOES NOT DO WHAT IT SAYS: the length backstop. The plan says: bring the longest share to 35 percent, then the shortest share. A drop for the shortest share makes the set smaller, so the longest share can rise above 35 percent again (seen in a made-up case). ob_select.py repeats the two steps until both shares are at or under the cap, with one seeded source per set. The plan text should say this.

READING CHOSEN: an HTTP 200 reply from DeepSeek is final, readable or not (content_retries is 0). FILE_FORMATS.md 6.2 says 'a readable reply is not asked again', which could be read as asking again after an unreadable one. Any other HTTP status leaves the item open, and the decide step refuses while an item is open. A service that keeps refusing one item would block the build and need a decision.

READING CHOSEN: solver item numbers go on within a set and mode (Q0001 to Q0003 for DeepSeek, then Q0004 on the first Claude sheet). FILE_FORMATS.md says 'number them from 1'. Numbering from 1 on every sheet would let a misfiled answer sheet be read as valid.
READING CHOSEN: 'fix-split' needs seal step 3A first (pipeline table: 3A, then 3B). This matches tools/ob_seal.py as read.
READING CHOSEN: in the anchor check the related thing is compared only for Noetics whose printed fields include relative_to (^4, ^6, ^7, ^8, ^9).
READING CHOSEN: when a batch reply is unreadable twice, each of its passages gets status BAD_OBJECT. MISSING is used when the reply was readable but had no object for that passage.

PLAN IS SILENT: the practice plain-fact floor (20). The reserve rule covers role-step tasks only. If the role-step floor is met and fewer than 20 practice plain-fact tasks survive, ob_select.py prints STOP_DO_NOT_LAUNCH.

result.what_was_built:
Four tools. All four parse. All four ran on a made-up fixture with no outside call, no key and no AWS. The parts that talk to DeepSeek and Gemini were read, not run.

CLAIM STATES
- REAL: the dry run on made-up passages (numbers below), and four read-only checks on the sibling's real role notes.
- NOT RUN: any real call to DeepSeek or Gemini. That code is wired only.
- Nothing here is a result about roles. No outcome code exists.

1. tools/ob_write_ordinary_notes.py (the rival's notes)
- Refuses to run unless the seal steps for that set's questions and keys exist (practice: 1, 2, 3A, 3B; final: also 3C). Refuses to write once seal step 4 exists.
- DeepSeek deepseek-chat, temperature 0, one passage per call. Two briefs, word for word from PLAN_CONSTANTS.json. Three lengths (090, 100, 110) by the plan formula N = (percent * C_role * W_p + 50 * M_p) // (100 * M_p).
- The prompt holds the brief and the passage only. The tool keeps only id and text from eligibility.json, only the three size numbers from role_notes.json, only passage ids from the selection file.
- One rewrite only, and only when support_results has a failed first check for that note. It never reads the answer-leak screen.
- The call log is the record. The notes file is rebuilt from it at every start. Threads; clean stop on HTTP 429; stop on a refused key; a call budget (--max-calls).
- Key from the environment variable only. Never logged.

2. tools/ob_check_support.py (the support check, decision D6)
- Commands: gemini, export, import, decide, status.
- Gemini gemini-2.5-flash-lite in batches of 12 notes (the six notes of two passages), seeded batch order. The checker sees a neutral item id, the passage and the note only.
- An unreadable item is asked once more; still unreadable counts as FAIL.
- Daily cap: clean stop, time recorded. A refused call is not counted as a try.
- Fallback: export writes a text sheet for a Claude Sonnet text-only sub-agent. It is refused until 24 hours after the first daily-cap stop. Whole passages only. A passage never has two checkers. import reads the answer sheets.
- Round 2 checks rewritten notes. Passage status: ALL_PASS, REWRITE_NEEDED, UNCHECKED, DROPPED_SECOND_FAILURE.
- The checkpoint, item map and results are rebuilt from the call log and the sheets at every start.

3. tools/ob_screen_notes.py (the answer-leak screen)
- Rules (a) to (d) on every note of every group: FILLER, ROLE, MIXED, QUOTES-ONLY (frame text only) and all three lengths of both ordinary groups.
- A hit drops the passage for every group and is logged with group, length, rule and task. The tool calls nobody, so a hit can not cause a rewrite.
- Before trusting the blanked role-note text it checks it: filling the blanks with the entry's own quotes must give back the note line.
- Prints passages and tasks left, re-checks the launch floor, prints the tier. Exit code 3 when the floor is missed.

4. tools/ob_assemble.py
- Keeps a passage only if it carries a task, passed the support check and was not hit.
- Sets letters last by the seeded rule. Writes prompts/prompt_parts_practice.json and prompts/prompt_parts_final.json, the two key files, the two task-facts files, review/review_pack.json, removal_log.json.
- Final prompt parts hold no key. The only right letter in any prompt part is the practice-only ANSWER-GIVEN note.
- Checks every canon line in ROLE and MIXED notes, letter for letter, against Part A of the guide (read, not retyped).
- Writes the list of planned calls and checks it against the cap of 5,000. Writes a manifest with one sha256 per file for seal step 5.
- If the floor is missed or the calls are above the cap, it writes the removal log only and exits with code 3.
- No code path for ROLE-PLAIN (D1).

FILES (all under C:/Users/wakil/OneDrive/Desktop/tksCAS/cas_only_reasoner/CASALESCENCE_NOETICS_v0_1/optionb/job/)

1. scorer_v0_1_1.py. Rules 0.1 with the one fix: a repeated key is FORMAT_FAIL, found with an object_pairs_hook. Same five categories and the same function names as tools/scorer_v0_1.py. Added: clean_reply, not_clean_reply, check_known_examples.

3. gate_b1.py. Standard library only. It holds the shared call plan (call ids, seeded task order, practice steps P1 to P3, final blocks, planned call counts), the Gate 1 to 3 decision functions that run-practice also uses, and Gates 0 to 7 with every number read from PLAN_CONSTANTS.json. It writes GATE.json once and prints the two no-rule extras.

4. analysis_b1.py. Pure standard library. Validity V1 to V3, readability R1 to R3 (5 points AND the test, D9), conditions C1 to C5, no-harm H1 and H2 with NOT_MEASURABLE, the outcome codes in checking order, the _EXPLORATORY rule, the number X, the fixed sentences, four sub-views, and the extra views. Whole-number counts only; a share is [part, whole]; a decimal is text; an empty share is the text "undefined"; written with allow_nan=False. After a gate stop it writes kind STOP with the stop code and no table. It also holds the package-against-seal check and the model-receipt check.
   Sign-flip test: random.Random(20261005); per flip r = getrandbits(number of passages); flipped sum = real sum minus 2 times the sum of d over flipped passages, worked out with one mask-and-bit-count per distinct value of d. Range: random.Random(20261005); 10,000 times rng.choices(passages, k=n); sorted values at index 250 and 9749; one-sided upper at index 9499.
   Operation count (EXPECTED): one test is 100,000 flips of at most about 15 small steps each, whatever the passage count. One range is at most 1.56 million draws (156 passages). One full run is at most 47 tests and 56 ranges: about 7 x 10^7 flip steps and 9 x 10^7 draws. EXPECTED 10 to 20 seconds for the real final set, 3 to 10 seconds per made-up set. The score limit is at least 120 seconds.

5. runner_b1.py. One file, five commands: selftest, run-practice, gate, run-final, score. Standard library plus torch and transformers. torch is imported only in mode gate0 and in the two run commands.
   - selftest does all of Gate 0 and writes selftest.json, padding_plan.json, prompt_hashes.jsonl and the trial_<SET>_* files. In mode precheck it loads the tokenizer only. Check order is the ten names of FILE_FORMATS 17.1.
   - run-practice: P1, decision line, P2, decision line with early_stop, then P3 only if Gates 2 and 3 pass.
   - run-final: only if GATE.json says go. It is given --constants and --prompts. It opens no key file. Block MUST_RUN, then NO-PASSAGE if GATE.json lists it. No ROLE-PLAIN path exists; an unknown group raises an error.
   - score: calls analysis_b1.run with the two receipt paths.
   - Each prompt is rebuilt and its sha256 must equal the dry-build hash before the model is called. One line per call is written, flushed and fsynced.
   - Decoding: a plain greedy loop copied from the pilot's proven call (argmax, use_cache=False, logits_to_keep=1, eager attention, float32, at most 64 new tokens, stop at an end token, no retry). GPU_REQUIRED on a CPU.
   - File rules: every write goes through create_once (mode xb), LineFile (xb, then add and fsync) or StatusLog (ab). No rename, delete, temporary file or link. sys.dont_write_bytecode is set first in every program, because the guest draft fails the stage if __pycache__ appears under the sealed source folder.

PLACES WHERE I HAD TO INTERPRET THE DESIGN (for the reviewers)
1. Random source: Python's random.Random, not numpy (see open issue 1).
2. Standard error: standard deviation divided by the count (numpy's default). Resampled differences are kept as millionths of a point, rounded down. Texts are rounded half away from zero to two decimals.
3. Practice lines missing, so a gate can not be worked out: stop code GATE_STOP_TIME if run-practice recorded STOP_WORK_CUTOFF, otherwise GATE_STOP_SELFTEST, with a detail text. The gate disagreeing with practice_decisions.jsonl: GATE_STOP_SELFTEST. A self-test status of GPU_REQUIRED becomes GATE_STOP_SELFTEST in GATE.json and RESULT.json, with GPU_REQUIRED in the detail.
4. No usable GATE.json at score time: the stop code of selftest.json if it has one, otherwise GATE_STOP_SELFTEST.
5. run-practice needs SELFTEST_PASS and mode gate0. Mode gate0 fails with GATE_STOP_SELFTEST if the two expected hashes are not given.
6. A plain-fact task always has level 1 in its call id, also when level 2 is chosen.
7. P1 and P2 use the seeded practice task order; in P1 the three wordings of a task sit back to back.
8. Padding target: the largest block over the passage's own groups (the must-run groups its tasks have). ANSWER-GIVEN is padded to that target but does not set it. Its average is reported too.
9. Self-test status: the first failed check decides. GATE_STOP_PADDING only when the 10% rule is the only fault of the padding check.
10. prompt_hashes.jsonl covers ANSWER-GIVEN and NO-PASSAGE at both levels and all three wordings for practice role-step tasks, and NO-PASSAGE for final role-step tasks.
11. Seconds per call cover build, tokenize, generate and decode. No warm-up call is made. Gate 7 rounds "now" up by one second.
12. End tokens come from the model's generation settings, else from the tokenizer.
13. Sub-views run the same nine comparisons as the main view. The two format-gap tests of R2 run on the main view only.
14. No-harm sentence: X is the index-9499 value of the resampled H1 loss, rounded up to a whole point, never below 0. H2 for QUOTES-ONLY uses role-step tasks only.
15. Outputs missing: INVALID_RUN and no comparison is worked out. A repeated call id also fails V1.
16. V2 checks the prompt hash of every final line, re-hashes the prompt text, and checks that prompt_hashes.jsonl still has the sha256 the self-test recorded.
17. Near miss: brackets, dots, colons and spaces are dropped at both ends. Letter counts cover clean replies only.
18. The self-test hashes the six small model files against the pins. In gate0 it checks only the size of model.safetensors. Final keys are hashed as bytes for the seal check and never parsed in the self-test.
19. A passage with no task is counted, not failed.
20. Extra views are each guarded: an error in one can not block the outcome code, but any such error fails the self-test.
21. The made-up clock (0 and 1000000), wording 1 and the malformed text are fixed in the runner; the self-test fails if the plan's recipe text for ALL_MALFORMED differs.
22. scorer: nesting too deep to parse is FORMAT_FAIL (the value would not be an allowed value anyway).

deviations_from_design_and_why: Setup flag is also set after a self-test STOP (not only after a pass). Why: the task rule that a gate stop must still be archived and uploaded; without the flag the controller ends the host at minute 30. After a self-test crash or an unreadable selftest.json the flag is not set and no model stage starts.

One guest mode only. My first draft also had a pre-check mode. I removed it when I saw that another builder gives the pre-check job its own supervisor (precheck_cpu/). The builders therefore make the GPU package only; build_input_zip_b1.py always copies all 7 model files.
The guest does not create work/run_b1. The runner creates it, exactly as in the pre-check job, so the GPU job starts from the state the pre-check has already run.

Added an early file-rule check after the self-test and before any model call: nothing new under work/source or work/external-authority, and only letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore in file names under work/run_b1. Why: the design names the file rules as one of the six things; a break found here costs no task.

Authority check changed instead of kept (the design allowed either). The flag mechanical_stage_binding_authorized is gone, because this guest writes no stage permits. The contract must now name external_authority.owner_record among its authority files.

Contract schema renamed to cas-optionb-b1-guest-contract/v1, and two blocks added that the guest checks: clock_seconds (must equal the guest's clock) and precheck (the two hashes of seal step 7). Why: an old contract can not be taken by mistake, and the pre-check binding of decision D7 has to reach Gate 0 somehow; the package itself is frozen before the pre-check runs.
The runner's command lines sit in one table (RUNNER) at the top of the guest, and all numbers are plain constants there. Why: the text check can read them by parsing, without running the guest.

Completeness is tied to 'a model stage was started' (run_practice or run_final) plus the result file, not to the final stage alone. Why: a crash in practice with no RESULT.json should also count as incomplete evidence.

After a crashed or timed-out model stage the guest starts no further model stage, but still hashes the model and runs score. Why: fail closed on spending tasks, and the design says the score command writes RESULT.json in every case.

build_contract_b1.py also stamps the guest's four source pins. Why: the guest keeps hard pins on the package, as the old one did, and they can not be known before source.zip exists. The stamp refuses a guest already stamped with other values.
source.zip is stored, not compressed. Why: the same bytes on any machine and any zlib version, so the pinned hash can be rebuilt. EXPECTED size 2 to 3 MB, far under every cap.

The builders write small receipts next to their outputs (SOURCE_ZIP_BUILD_RECEIPT.json, CONTRACT_BUILD_RECEIPT.json, INPUT_ZIP_BUILD_RECEIPT.json) and text_check_b1.py --write saves TEXT_CHECK_B1.json. findings.where: selection.letters.rule (line 531). Plan section 10 Step 6 item 4 (line 470). tools/ob_assemble.py line 542.
findings.problem: The letters rule favors the letter A, and the plan's sentence about it is false. Within every type and level the right letters are dealt 'in turn' and every type starts again at A. So A gets the extra task in every type whose count is not a multiple of 4 (or 6). The surplus adds up over the six types. 'Always answer A' then scores above chance. Gate 2's lower edge (chance plus 10 points) and Gate 6 (chance plus 15 points) are written against true chance, so a model that leans to A, as small models often do, gets a head start on a 36 to 50 task practice set.
findings.evidence: Constants: 'give the right option the letters in turn (A, B, C, D or A to F)'. ob_assemble.py line 542: 'right_letter = letters[index % shown]' with index starting at 0 for every type and level. Plan line 470: 'So "always answer A" scores exactly chance.' My arithmetic (REAL): types with 5, 9, 6, 7, 5, 4 tasks (36) make A right on 12 (33.3%) and D on 7 (19.4%). Types with 5, 5, 5, 5, 9, 9 tasks (38) make A right on 14 (36.8%), which is above Gate 2's lower edge of 35%. EXPECTED average surplus for A: 0.375 task per type, about 2 tasks over six types. The comparison between groups is not biased, because every group has the same letters.
findings.fix: Before the seal, change the rule so the surplus does not pile up on A. PROPOSED: per set, family and level, join the per-type shuffled lists in type order and deal the letters in turn across the whole joined list, without starting again at A for each type. Then each letter is right equally often to within one task inside every type and over the whole set. Change selection.letters.rule, ob_assemble.py set_letters and its balance check, and replace 'exactly chance' by 'chance to within one task'.

findings.where: Section 15.4 (line 821) and section 21 'Spec sheet' (line 1149).

REAL, counted by me on optionb/dry/elig/eligibility.json: of the 190 eligible passages that are not barred, 0 hold the word answer, 0 hold option, 4 hold correct. findings.problem: The tool does what the plan says and nothing more. The risk is in the rule and in when it can first be measured. EXPECTED, NOT MEASURED. findings.where: PLAN_CONSTANTS.json lines 709 and 715 to 717 (block "tests"), against optionb/job/analysis_b1.py lines 259 to 313 (sign_flip_counts, bootstrap_points)
findings.problem: The constants file and the analysis program name two different random procedures for the one test that decides every outcome code. The constants say numpy PCG64 with a fixed draw recipe. The program uses the Python standard library (Mersenne Twister, getrandbits and choices). The two give different flip counts. Near the line of 5,000 flips they can give different answers to 'X beats Y'. PLAN_CONSTANTS.json is sealed in step 1. If it is sealed as it stands, the sealed plan describes a test that was not run, and after the data exist someone could run the registered recipe and get another count.
